gate.gate_text: For BOTH of leg 360's two non-effective ingredients in delta_0 = K_H^{-1} K_2^{-1} * theta_*^2/8 (CKN's epsilon_*, and the Harnack constant K_H cited to Gilbarg-Trudinger Corollary 9.25), does a literature search locate a published source with an explicit numeric or formula-level value, checked clause-by-clause for reach into Pineau-Vicol's actual usage context?
gate.answer: YES, both constants adjudicated to a definite per-constant verdict: NO-EXPLICIT-VALUE-LOCATED for epsilon_*, NO-EXPLICIT-VALUE-LOCATED for K_H. The search is recorded honestly with links (not counts) for what was found that did not reach, and refusals (empty-result searches) banked as refusals, not silently omitted.
gate.consequence_for_delta0: BLOCKED (not COMPUTABLE, not BOUNDABLE-ONLY-beyond-leg-360's-formula) -- no new numeric or closed-form reduction was located beyond leg 360's formula-level dependency chain. delta_0 remains exactly where leg 360 left it: a formula, one link short of a number, for both of its non-constructive ingredients.
gate.independent_second_blocker_restated: Regardless of this leg's findings on delta_0, leg 360 separately found (its Condition 1 / Section 3) that the pressure-decay hypothesis eq:local:pbound does NOT close under Pineau-Vicol's own class-wide pressure-decay estimate substituted via their own change of variables: |p(x,t)| <~ C_{P,0}(sigma)*(-t)^{-sigma/2}, which DIVERGES as t -> 0- for every sigma > 0 the paper's estimate ever attains (sigma=0 is never reached). This is a SEPARATE, INDEPENDENT gap from delta_0's non-explicitness. Even if delta_0 became fully numerically computable, the screen would still be blocked by this pressure-decay divergence unless that is separately resolved -- which is not this leg's task and was not attempted here.

constant_1_epsilon_star.role: Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg epsilon-regularity threshold constant, cited by Pineau-Vicol at Liouvillev2.tex l.1994-1995 to [CKN82, Lin98, LadySeregin99, Kukavica09]
constant_1_epsilon_star.pv_usage_context_quoted: "there exists a universal constant $\eps_*>0$ such that if $\limsup_{r\to 0^+} \frac 1r \int_{Q_r}\|\nabla u\|^2 \leq \eps_*$, then $(0,0)$ is a regular point" -- l.1994-1995, re-verified this leg by re-downloading and grepping Liouvillev2.tex (sha256 matched leg 360's pin exactly)
constant_1_epsilon_star.usage_class: the classical Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg local energy epsilon-regularity criterion for suitable weak solutions of the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations (not a CKN functional/interpolation inequality -- a distinct, commonly confused body of literature under the same author-triple name, screened out of this search)

load_bearing_find.paper: Zhen Lei, Xiao Ren, "Quantitative partial regularity of the Navier-Stokes equations and applications", arXiv:2210.01783v1 (4 Oct 2022)
load_bearing_find.fetched_and_read: PDF fetched, converted with pdftotext, 4155 lines, grepped for 'explicit'/'numerical value'/'effective constant'
load_bearing_find.what_it_actually_shows_quoted: "Note that the methods in [20, 17] rely on certain (non-quantitative) compactness arguments, while the method in [35] based on the De Giorgi iteration is quantitative." [35] = Alexis F. Vasseur, "A new proof of partial regularity of solutions to Navier-Stokes equations", NoDEA Nonlinear Differential Equations Appl. 14(5-6):753-785, 2007 (not on arXiv). [20] = Fanghua Lin's proof, [17] = Ladyzhenskaya-Seregin's proof -- both cited generically and non-quantitatively.
load_bearing_find.key_negative_finding: "We point out that the proof of Theorem 4 in [3] is still non-quantitative, essentially because the absolute continuity of the dissipation energy is a non-quantitative fact. ... it is clearly impossible to give an explicit dependence of delta on epsilon unless higher integrability of g is assumed." ([3] = the original 1982 Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg paper)
load_bearing_find.lei_ren_s_own_theorem_6_quoted: "Theorem 6 (CKN criterion). Let v be a local suitable weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations in Q(1). There exists a universal positive constant epsilon** such that limsup(1/r) int_{Q(r)} |grad v|^2 dxdt <= epsilon** implies (0,0) not in S[v]."
load_bearing_find.verdict_on_this_source: even Lei-Ren 2022 -- the most recent, most directly relevant paper located, explicitly built on the ONE 'quantitative' (non-compactness) proof route that exists in this literature (Vasseur's De Giorgi iteration) -- states only EXISTENCE of a 'universal positive constant epsilon**'. No numeric value, no closed-form formula in terms of any base quantities, is ever written down. 'Quantitative' here is used by the authors to mean the DERIVATION avoids non-constructive compactness/contradiction steps, not that a number is supplied.

reach_check_clause_by_clause.equation_class_matches: YES -- suitable weak solutions of 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes, same theorem family PV cite (Lin98, LadySeregin99 are literally two of the four PV citations; Lei-Ren's [20],[17] are the same works)
reach_check_clause_by_clause.quantitative_route_cited_by_PV: NO -- PV's own citation list at l.1994-1995 is exactly [CKN82, Lin98, LadySeregin99, Kukavica09] -- all four are non-quantitative/compactness-based in Lei-Ren's own classification. PV do not cite Vasseur or any De Giorgi-iteration-based (quantitative-route) proof at all.
reach_check_clause_by_clause.does_a_number_exist_anywhere_in_the_quan: NO, as far as this leg's search reached -- not in Vasseur's paper itself (not accessible on arXiv to re-verify directly, but its own status as merely 'quantitative-in-derivation' rather than 'numerically explicit' is independently confirmed by Lei-Ren's own reading and by Lei-Ren's own inheritance of a bare-existence Theorem 6), and not in Lei-Ren's 2022 paper, its most recent published descendant.

constant_1_epsilon_star.consequence: Even setting aside that PV do not cite the (only) quantitative-derivation route, that route's own literature -- checked to its most recent 2022 representative -- has never itself produced a number. This constant remains a bare existence statement everywhere this leg searched.

constant_2_K_H_harnack.role: Harnack constant for the uniformly elliptic (non-divergence-form) operator L_bar* - lambda_Rbar, cited by Pineau-Vicol at Liouvillev2.tex l.2063-2065 to Gilbarg-Trudinger Corollary 9.25
constant_2_K_H_harnack.pv_usage_context_quoted: "By Harnack's inequality for the uniformly elliptic operator $\bar L^*-\lambda_{\bar R}$ (see e.g. [Corollary 9.25]{GilbargTrudinger98}), there exists a constant $K_H = K_H(R_{**},C_u)>0$" -- l.2063-2065, re-verified this leg by re-downloading and grepping Liouvillev2.tex (sha256 matched leg 360's pin exactly)
constant_2_K_H_harnack.operator_form_traced_this_leg: PV define their operator earlier (l.720) as $\mathcal{L} := -a^{ij}\partial_{ij} + b^i\partial_i + c$ -- an explicitly NON-DIVERGENCE-FORM operator (second derivative acted on directly, not $\partial_i(a^{ij}\partial_j \cdot)$) with smooth symmetric coefficients $a^{ij}$, smooth bounded drift $b^i$, and a potential $c \geq 0$ -- this is the setting of Gilbarg-Trudinger's Chapter 9 ('Strong Solutions', the Krylov-Safonov / Aleksandrov-Bakelman-Pucci circle of results for non-divergence-form operators), consistent with the citation to a Chapter-9 corollary rather than a Chapter-8 (divergence-form, De Giorgi-Nash-Moser) result
